items.prompt: While Tom was walking along the beach, he found an old coin. → ___ along the beach, Tom found an old coin.
items.why: He found it while he was walking: same time and active, so -ing.

items.prompt: Because she was shocked by the news, Priya sat down. → ___ by the news, Priya sat down.
items.why: Priya feels the shock, it is done to her: -ed.

items.prompt: After he had finished the report, Kwame went home. → ___ the report, Kwame went home.
items.why: He finished first and went home after: having + -ed.

items.prompt: Because he didn't know the way, Liam asked a taxi driver. → ___ the way, Liam asked a taxi driver.
items.why: Put not before the participle: Not knowing.

items.prompt: Because she was tired after the flight, Mei went straight to bed. → ___ after the flight, Mei went straight to bed.
items.why: Tired is an adjective that describes Mei. Tiring means that something makes you tired.

items.prompt: When she was asked about the plan, Olga refused to comment. → When ___ about the plan, Olga refused to comment.
items.why: Someone asked Olga: passive meaning, so -ed.

items.prompt: Diego checked the windows before he left the flat. → Before ___ the flat, Diego checked the windows.
items.why: After before / after / while use the -ing form.

items.prompt: Because he had forgotten his umbrella, Kwame got soaked. → ___ his umbrella, Kwame got soaked.
items.why: The forgetting came first, the soaking after: having + -ed.
